records.gloss: How blessed [are the] blameless of way, the [ones] walking in [the] instruction of YHWH!
pieces: How blessed are those whose way of life is without fault, who walk by the instruction of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!

L.1: How blessed [are] the blameless in [their] way, who walk in the instruction of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!

R.1: Life is truly good for people who live without blame and follow the teaching of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Psalm 119: an alphabet poem in twenty-two stanzas
decisions.reason: The psalm is an acrostic, the longest in the Bible. It has twenty-two stanzas, one for each letter of the Hebrew alphabet, and each of the eight verses of a stanza begins with that letter. The first stanza (verses 1-8) begins with aleph. Nearly every verse names God's law with one of eight words (instruction, testimonies, precepts, statutes, commands, judgments, word, saying), and each is given the same wording throughout. The psalm has no title.

decisions.choice: How blessed: an exclamation about a life that goes well
decisions.reason: The word ('ashre) is an exclamation: "oh, the blessings of ...". It speaks of the well-being of a life in step with God, as in 1:1. Psalm 119 opens like Psalm 1.
The word (tamim) means whole or sound, a life with nothing crooked in it. It does not claim that these people never sin (verse 176).
To walk in God's instruction is to live by it, a picture used all through the psalm.

The word (torah) means instruction or teaching, from a verb for pointing out the way. It is the first of eight words for God's law that run through this psalm, and covers all that God has taught his people, not only the rules of the law of Moses.
As in 1:1, Literal and Balanced keep the exclamation.
As in 1:1, Readable says what the word means.
As in the earlier psalms, Literal and Balanced say "instruction" and Readable "teaching"; "law" can sound like a legal code only. The psalm uses the same word for torah throughout.

records.heading: Your word, my delight and my life

records.gloss: How blessed [are those] keeping his testimonies; with all [the] heart they seek him.
pieces: How blessed are those who hold fast to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} decrees and seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with their whole heart.

L.2: How blessed [are] those who keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} testimonies; with all [the] heart they seek {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.2: Life is truly good for people who do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has declared and who turn to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all their heart.

decisions.reason: As in 119:1.
The verb (natsar) is to guard or watch over something with care; here, to hold to what God has said and live by it.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
decisions.reason: The word ('edot, also 'edut) is related to the word for a witness: what God has solemnly declared and stands witness to, the terms of his covenant (Deuteronomy 4:45). It is one of the psalm's eight words for God's law.

decisions.choice: seek him: turn to God, want him
decisions.reason: To seek God (darash) is to turn to him in prayer and worship and to want to know him, not to look for something lost.

decisions.choice: testimonies (L); decrees (B); what you have declared (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "testimonies", close to the word's root. Balanced says "decrees" and Readable says plainly what they are. The psalm uses the same wording for this word throughout.
Readable says what seeking God means here.

records.gloss: Also they do not do injustice; in his ways they walk.
pieces: They do nothing crooked; they keep to the ways {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shown.

L.3: Indeed, they do no wrong; in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways they walk.

R.3: They do not do what is wrong. They live the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants them to.

decisions.reason: The word ('awlah) is what is twisted or unjust, especially wrong done to others.

decisions.choice: walk in his ways: live as God directs
decisions.reason: God's ways are the paths of life he has shown his people (Deuteronomy 8:6).

decisions.choice: the ways he has shown (B); the way he wants (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose ways these are and what they are.

records.gloss: You, you have commanded your precepts to keep [them] very much.
pieces: You have laid down {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts to be kept with all care.

L.4: You have commanded {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts, to keep [them] diligently.

R.4: You gave {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions so that we would obey them with great care.

decisions.choice: You: the psalm turns to speak to God
decisions.reason: Verses 1-3 speak about God; from here on the psalm speaks to him almost throughout. The pronoun is emphatic: it is God himself who gave these precepts.

decisions.choice: precepts: the charges God has laid down
decisions.reason: The word (piqqudim) is found only in the Psalms. It comes from a verb for appointing or putting in charge, so it means the particular charges God has given. It is one of the psalm's eight words for God's law.
The word (me'od) means "very, greatly"; with "keep" it means keeping them with great care.
Literal and Balanced say "precepts"; Readable says "instructions", a plainer word. The psalm keeps the same wording throughout.
Readable names who is to keep the precepts: God's people.

records.gloss: Oh that my ways were firm to keep your statutes!
pieces: If only my life were set firmly on keeping {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes!

L.5: Oh that my ways were made firm to keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes!

R.5: I wish I could always be steady in obeying {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws!

decisions.reason: The word ('achalay) expresses a longing: "if only".
The verb (kun) is to be firm or fixed; the psalmist longs for a life that does not waver.

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: The word (chuqqim; the related chuqqot in verse 16) comes from a verb for carving or marking out: a rule that stands fixed. It is one of the psalm's eight words for God's law.
Literal and Balanced say "statutes"; Readable says "laws", the everyday word. The psalm keeps the same wording throughout.

records.gloss: Then not I will be ashamed, when I look to all your commands.
pieces: Then I will not be put to shame, as I keep my eyes on all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

L.6: Then I will not be put to shame, when I look to all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

R.6: Then I will not be ashamed, because I will pay attention to all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

decisions.choice: be put to shame: be disgraced, be let down
decisions.reason: The verb (bosh) is to be disgraced, often by finding that what one trusted has failed.

decisions.choice: look to: pay attention to, consider
decisions.reason: The verb (hibbit) is to look at something closely and take it to heart.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: The word (mitsvot) comes from the verb "command" used in verse 4. It is one of the psalm's eight words for God's law.

records.source: א֭וֹדְךָ בְּיֹ֣שֶׁר לֵבָ֑ב בְּ֝לָמְדִ֗י מִשְׁפְּטֵ֥י צִדְקֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: I will thank you with uprightness of heart, when I learn [the] judgments of your righteousness.
pieces: With an honest heart I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks, as I come to learn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteous rulings.

L.7: I will give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with uprightness of heart, when I learn the judgments of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.

R.7: When I learn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions, which are always right, I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with an honest heart.

decisions.reason: The verb (hodah) is to give thanks by saying openly what God has done.

decisions.choice: judgments: God's rulings, his decisions about what is right
decisions.reason: The word (mishpatim) is a judge's verdict: the decisions God has made about what is right, which then guide how people live (Exodus 21:1). It is one of the psalm's eight words for God's law.

decisions.choice: judgments of your righteousness: your righteous rulings
decisions.reason: The second noun describes the first: rulings that are right and just.
"Judgments" can sound like punishments, so Balanced says "rulings" and Readable "decisions", which keep the sense of a judge's verdict. The psalm keeps the same wording throughout.

records.gloss: Your statutes I will keep; do not forsake me up to muchness.
pieces: I will hold to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes; do not leave me wholly alone.

L.8: Your statutes I will keep; do not forsake me utterly.

R.8: I will obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws. Please do not leave me on my own for good.

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.
The phrase ("up to muchness") means "to the full". The psalmist does not deny that trouble may come, but asks not to be left without God altogether.

decisions.choice: do not leave me on my own for good
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the request means.

records.gloss: By what will a youth keep his path pure? By keeping [it] according to your word.
pieces: How can the young keep their way of life clean? By taking care to live as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word directs.

L.9: By what will {{gender:a young person|a young man}} keep {{gender:their|his}} path pure? By keeping watch [over it] according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

R.9: How can young people keep their lives pure? They must watch how they live and do what {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word says.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter beth, the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1).
The word (na'ar) is masculine and means a boy or young man, but the question is asked for anyone young setting out in life, as in Proverbs 1:4.

decisions.choice: keep pure: keep clean, free of wrong
decisions.reason: The verb (zakah) is to be clean or pure, here of a way of life.
The verse asks a question and answers it: by keeping watch over one's path as God's word directs.
The word (davar) is anything spoken; here it is what God has said to his people. It is one of the psalm's eight words for God's law.

decisions.choice: a young person ... their; "a young man ... his" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The question is for anyone young (m2), so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default.
Balanced and Readable say it in the plural, which needs no setting.

records.gloss: With all my heart I have sought you; do not let me stray from your commands.
pieces: I have searched for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all my heart; do not let me drift away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

L.10: With all my heart I have sought {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; do not let me wander from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

R.10: I have looked for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all my heart. Do not let me wander away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

decisions.choice: sought you: turned to God, wanted him
decisions.reason: As in 119:2.

decisions.choice: wander: go astray, stray by mistake
decisions.reason: The verb (shagah) is used of straying without meaning to, as a sheep wanders off. The psalmist asks God to keep him from it.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: As in 119:6.

records.source: בְּ֭לִבִּי צָפַ֣נְתִּי אִמְרָתֶ֑ךָ לְ֝מַ֗עַן לֹ֣א אֶֽחֱטָא־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: In my heart I have hidden your saying, so that I may not sin against you.
pieces: Deep in my heart I have kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word safe, so that I will not sin against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.11: In my heart I have hidden {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying, so that I may not sin against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.11: I keep what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said close in my heart, to keep me from sinning against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.reason: The verb (tsafan) is to hide something away to keep it safe, as treasure is hidden (Proverbs 2:1; 10:14).

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often his promise
decisions.reason: The word ('imrah) comes from the verb "say": what God has said. In this psalm it often means a promise God has made (verses 38, 41, 50). It is one of the psalm's eight words for God's law.

decisions.choice: saying (L); promise, or word where no promise is in view (B); promise, or what you said (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps a word of its own for 'imrah, so that it can be told apart from davar ("word"). Balanced and Readable say "promise" where a promise is in view, and otherwise "word" (Balanced) or "what you said" (Readable).

records.gloss: Blessed [are] you, YHWH; teach me your statutes.
pieces: All praise to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! Teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

decisions.reason: This is a different word from "How blessed" in verses 1-2: baruk, said of God, means that he is praised and thanked (28:6; 41:14).

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.

decisions.choice: teach me your statutes: a request the psalm repeats
decisions.reason: The same request comes again in verses 26, 64, 68 and later in the psalm.

records.gloss: With my lips I recount all [the] judgments of your mouth.
pieces: Aloud I tell over every ruling {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken.

L.13: With my lips I recount all the judgments of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mouth.

R.13: I say out loud all the decisions {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken.

decisions.choice: recount: tell over, list one by one
decisions.reason: The verb (sipper) is to count out or tell in order.

decisions.choice: judgments: God's rulings, his decisions about what is right
decisions.reason: As in 119:7.

decisions.choice: of your mouth: that you have spoken
decisions.reason: God's mouth stands for what he has said.
Balanced and Readable say what the picture means.

records.gloss: In [the] way of your testimonies I rejoice, as over all wealth.
pieces: Following {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees gives me as much joy as all the riches in the world.

L.14: In the way of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies I rejoice, as over all riches.

R.14: Living by what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared makes me as happy as if I owned great riches.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
decisions.reason: As in 119:2.

decisions.choice: as over all wealth: as much as over every kind of riches
decisions.reason: The comparison means the psalmist is as glad as a person who had all wealth.
Balanced and Readable say what being in the way of the decrees means.

records.gloss: On your precepts I will meditate, and I will look at your paths.
pieces: I will think deeply about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts and keep my eyes on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways.

L.15: On {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts I will meditate, and I will look closely at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} paths.

R.15: I will think deeply about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions and pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways.

decisions.choice: precepts: the charges God has laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:4.

decisions.choice: meditate: think over, ponder, talk over
decisions.reason: The verb (siach) is to think something over, often aloud. It comes again in verses 23, 27, 48 and 78.

decisions.choice: look closely at: pay attention to
decisions.reason: As at 119:6.

records.gloss: In your statutes I will delight myself; I will not forget your word.
pieces: Your statutes are my joy; I will not let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word slip from my mind.

L.16: In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes I will delight; I will not forget {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

R.16: I enjoy {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws. I will not forget {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5. Here the Hebrew has the related feminine form (chuqqot), with the same meaning.
The verb (hishta'shea') is to take delight or play with joy. It comes again in verses 47 and 70, and the noun "delight" in verses 24 and 77.
As in 119:9.

records.gloss: Deal fully with your servant, [that] I may live and keep your word.
pieces: Treat {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant with kindness, and I will live and hold to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

L.17: Deal bountifully with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, [that] I may live and keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

R.17: Be good to me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, so that I can live and obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter gimel, the third letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1).
The verb (gamal) is to deal fully with someone, often to do them good (13:6; 116:7).

decisions.choice: your servant: the psalmist speaking of himself
decisions.reason: Calling oneself someone's servant was the humble way to speak to a king or to God. The psalmist does so often in this psalm.
As in 119:9.

records.gloss: Uncover my eyes, that I may look at wonderful [things] from your instruction.
pieces: Take the veil from my eyes, so that I may see the wonders in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

L.18: Uncover my eyes, that I may look at wonders out of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

R.18: Help me see clearly, so that I can find the amazing things in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.choice: uncover my eyes: let me see what is hidden
decisions.reason: The verb (galah) is to uncover or reveal. The psalmist asks God to take away whatever keeps him from seeing (Numbers 24:4).

decisions.choice: wonders: things too great for people to do or grasp
decisions.reason: The word (nifla'ot) is used of God's mighty deeds (9:2; 78:4). Here it is what God's instruction holds for the one whose eyes are opened.
As in 119:1.
Balanced keeps the picture of a covering taken away.
Readable says what the request means.

records.source: גֵּ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י בָאָ֑רֶץ אַל־תַּסְתֵּ֥ר מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי מִצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: A sojourner I [am] on the earth; do not hide from me your commands.
pieces: I am only a foreigner living on the earth; do not keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands hidden from me.

L.19: A sojourner I [am] on the earth; do not hide {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands from me.

R.19: I am like a visitor in this world. Do not keep me from knowing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

decisions.choice: sojourner: a foreigner living in a land not his own
decisions.reason: A sojourner (ger) lived among a people without land or family to protect him and depended on others' kindness. The psalmist feels his life on earth is like that (39:13), and so he needs God's commands to guide him.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: As in 119:6.
Readable uses a plain word and makes clear it is a picture.

records.gloss: My soul is crushed with longing for your judgments at every time.
pieces: I am worn thin by longing for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings, every hour.

L.20: My soul is crushed with longing for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments at all times.

R.20: I long for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions so much that it hurts, all the time.

decisions.reason: The verb (garas) is rare; it is used of teeth broken on gravel (Lamentations 3:16). The longing is so strong that it wears the psalmist down.

decisions.choice: judgments: God's rulings, his decisions about what is right
decisions.reason: As in 119:7.
As in the earlier psalms, Literal keeps "soul" (nefesh) and Balanced and Readable say what it means here, the whole person.

records.gloss: You rebuke [the] arrogant, cursed [ones], the [ones] straying from your commands.
pieces: You rebuke the proud, the people under a curse who wander away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

L.21: You rebuke the arrogant, the cursed, who wander from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

R.21: You scold proud people. They are under a curse, and they wander away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

decisions.reason: The word (zedim) is for people who are proud and act against God and others without fear. They come again in verses 51, 69, 78 and 85.
God's rebuke (ga'ar) is a stern word that stops and judges (9:6).

alternatives: You rebuke the arrogant. Cursed are those who wander ...
decisions.reason: "Cursed" may describe the arrogant, as the Hebrew accents take it, or begin a new sentence, as the ancient Greek translation reads it. The meaning is much the same.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: As in 119:6.

records.source: גַּ֣ל מֵֽ֭עָלַי חֶרְפָּ֣ה וָב֑וּז כִּ֖י עֵדֹתֶ֣יךָ נָצָֽרְתִּי׃
records.gloss: Roll away from on me scorn and contempt, for your testimonies I have kept.
pieces: Lift insult and contempt off me, for I have held to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees.

L.22: Roll away from me scorn and contempt, for I have kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies.

R.22: Take away the insults and the scorn people heap on me. I have done what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared.

decisions.choice: roll away from on me: take off me
decisions.reason: Scorn and contempt are pictured as a weight lying on the psalmist (Joshua 5:9).
As in 119:2.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
decisions.reason: As in 119:2.
Readable says where the scorn comes from.

records.source: גַּ֤ם יָֽשְׁב֣וּ שָׂ֭רִים בִּ֣י נִדְבָּ֑רוּ עַ֝בְדְּךָ֗ יָשִׂ֥יחַ בְּחֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Even [though] officials sit, against me they speak together; your servant meditates on your statutes.
pieces: Even when men in power sit and talk against me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant keeps thinking about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

L.23: Even [though] officials sit [and] talk together against me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant meditates on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

R.23: Leaders get together and talk against me, but I, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, keep thinking about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.reason: The word (sarim) is used of royal officials and leaders.

decisions.choice: talk together against me: plot, slander
decisions.reason: The verb (nidbar) is to speak with one another, here against the psalmist.

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.

records.gloss: Also your testimonies [are] my delight, the men of my counsel.
pieces: Yes, I delight in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees; they are the advisers I listen to.

L.24: Indeed, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies [are] my delight, the men of my counsel.

R.24: What {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared makes me glad. It gives me the advice I need.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
decisions.reason: As in 119:2.

decisions.choice: delight: joy, what one takes pleasure in
decisions.reason: The noun (sha'ashu'im) is related to the verb in verse 16.

decisions.choice: the men of my counsel: my advisers
decisions.reason: While officials talk against him (verse 23), the psalmist's counselors are God's decrees.

decisions.choice: the advisers I listen to (B); the advice I need (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the phrase means.

records.gloss: My soul clings to the dust; give me life according to your word.
pieces: I lie pressed down in the dust; give me life, as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word has said.

L.25: My soul clings to the dust; give me life according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

R.25: I am close to death. Keep me alive, just as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word says.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter daleth, the fourth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1).

decisions.choice: clings to the dust: lies near death, brought low
decisions.reason: To lie in the dust is to be humbled and close to the grave (22:16; 44:26).

decisions.choice: give me life: keep me alive, renew my life
decisions.reason: The verb (chayyah, give life) is to keep alive, to bring back to life, or to renew someone's strength. The psalmist is close to death (verse 25) and asks God to keep him alive.
As in 119:9.
As in the earlier psalms, Literal keeps "soul" (nefesh) and Balanced and Readable say what it means here, the whole person.

alternatives: my soul clings to the dust
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means.

records.gloss: My ways I recounted, and you answered me; teach me your statutes.
pieces: I laid my life out before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave me an answer; teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

L.26: My ways I recounted, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} answered me; teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

R.26: I told {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} everything I had done, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} answered. Now teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.reason: The verb is the one in verse 13. Telling God one's ways may include confessing them.

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.

decisions.choice: laid my life out (B); everything I had done (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "my ways" means.

records.gloss: [The] way of your precepts make me understand, and I will meditate on your wonders.
pieces: Help me grasp the path {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts mark out, and I will ponder {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonderful deeds.

L.27: The way of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts make me understand, and I will meditate on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders.

R.27: Help me understand what {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions are showing me, and I will think about the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done.

decisions.choice: precepts: the charges God has laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:4.
The word is the one in verse 18; here it may mean God's mighty deeds (as in 9:2) or the wonders found in his instruction.

records.gloss: My soul weeps from grief; raise me up according to your word.
pieces: I am melting away in sorrow; lift me up as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word has said.

L.28: My soul weeps from grief; raise me up according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

R.28: I am so sad that I cry and cry. Make me strong again, just as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word says.

decisions.reason: The verb (dalaf) is to drip, as a roof leaks (Ecclesiastes 10:18); here of a person wasting away in tears.
The verb (qiyyem) is to make stand, to set someone on their feet.
As in 119:9.
As in the earlier psalms, Literal keeps "soul" (nefesh) and Balanced and Readable say what it means here, the whole person.

records.gloss: [The] way of falsehood remove from me, and [with] your instruction be gracious to me.
pieces: Keep me far from every false path, and be gracious to me by giving me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

L.29: The way of falsehood remove from me, and graciously [give] me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

R.29: Keep me from living a lie. Be kind to me and give me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.reason: The word (sheqer) is what is false, whether lies told or a life built on them. The way of falsehood is set against the way of faithfulness in verse 30.

decisions.choice: be gracious to me with your instruction
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "your instruction be gracious to me": God's instruction is the gift the psalmist asks for.
As in 119:1.
Literal supplies the verb the sense needs (m2).

records.gloss: [The] way of faithfulness I have chosen; your judgments I have set [before me].
pieces: The path of faithfulness is the one I have chosen; I have set {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings in front of me.

L.30: The way of faithfulness I have chosen; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments I have set [before me].

R.30: I have decided to live a faithful life. I keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions always in front of me.

decisions.reason: The word ('emunah) is steadiness and faithfulness, the opposite of the false way in verse 29.

decisions.choice: set before me: keep in view
decisions.reason: The verb (shivvah) is to set or place; with the same verb in 16:8 the psalmist sets the LORD before him. Here he keeps God's rulings in view.

decisions.choice: judgments: God's rulings, his decisions about what is right
decisions.reason: As in 119:7.

records.gloss: I have clung to your testimonies, YHWH; do not put me to shame.
pieces: I have held tight to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; let me not be disgraced.

L.31: I have clung to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; do not put me to shame.

R.31: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I hold on tight to what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared. Do not let me be ashamed.

decisions.reason: The verb (davaq) is the one in verse 25: the psalmist's soul clings to the dust, but he clings to God's decrees.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
decisions.reason: As in 119:2.
As in 119:6.

records.gloss: [The] way of your commands I will run, for you enlarge my heart.
pieces: I will run along the path of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} open my heart wide.

L.32: The way of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands I will run, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} enlarge my heart.

R.32: I will run to do what {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands say, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set me free inside.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: As in 119:6.

decisions.choice: enlarge my heart: set free, give room and understanding
decisions.reason: A heart made wide is the opposite of a heart hemmed in by distress (25:17). It may also mean a mind given understanding, as God gave Solomon "breadth of heart".
The word (ki) may give the reason ("for") or the time ("when").
Readable says one sense of the picture (m2).

records.source: הוֹרֵ֣נִי יְ֭הוָה דֶּ֥רֶךְ חֻקֶּ֗יךָ וְאֶצְּרֶ֥נָּה עֵֽקֶב׃
records.gloss: Teach me, YHWH, [the] way of your statutes, and I will keep it [to the] end.
pieces: Show me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the path of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes, and I will hold to it to the very end.

L.33: Teach me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the way of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes, and I will keep it to the end.

R.33: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show me how to live by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws, and I will obey them to the end.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter he, the fifth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1). Most of them begin with a request in the same verb form ("teach me", "give me understanding", "lead me").
The verb (horah) is to point the way; the word torah (instruction) comes from it.

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.

decisions.choice: to the end: always, all the way
decisions.reason: The word ('eqev) means the end or result of something, and also a reward (19:12). Here it probably means keeping God's way to the end.

records.gloss: Give me understanding, and I will keep your instruction and observe it with all [the] heart.
pieces: Make me understand, and I will guard {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction and keep it wholeheartedly.

L.34: Give me understanding, and I will keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction and observe it with all [the] heart.

R.34: Help me understand, and I will follow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching and obey it with my whole heart.

decisions.choice: give me understanding: make me understand
decisions.reason: The verb (hevin) is to make someone understand, to give insight.
As in 119:1.

decisions.choice: keep ... observe: two verbs for one resolve
decisions.reason: The verbs (natsar, shamar) both mean to guard and keep; together they say the psalmist will hold to God's instruction fully.

records.gloss: Lead me in [the] path of your commands, for in it I delight.
pieces: Guide me along the track of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, for that is where my delight is.

L.35: Make me walk in the path of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, for in it I delight.

R.35: Lead me on the path of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, because I love to go that way.

decisions.choice: make me walk: lead, guide my steps
decisions.reason: The verb (hidrik) is to make someone tread a way.
The word (netiv) is a beaten track, narrower than a road.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: As in 119:6.
The verb (chafets) is to want and enjoy something.

records.gloss: Turn my heart to your testimonies and not to unjust gain.
pieces: Bend my heart toward {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees, not toward greedy profit.

L.36: Turn my heart to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies, and not to unjust gain.

R.36: Make me want what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared, not money I grab for myself.

decisions.reason: The verb (hittah) is to bend or stretch something toward a place: the psalmist asks God to set the direction of his desires.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
decisions.reason: As in 119:2.

decisions.choice: unjust gain: profit got by greed or force
decisions.reason: The word (betsa') is profit taken wrongly, by greed, bribery or violence (Proverbs 1:19; Isaiah 33:15).
Readable says what turning the heart means.

records.source: הַעֲבֵ֣ר עֵ֭ינַי מֵרְא֣וֹת שָׁ֑וְא בִּדְרָכֶ֥ךָ חַיֵּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Make my eyes pass from seeing worthlessness; in your ways give me life.
pieces: Turn my eyes from gazing at empty things; keep me alive as I walk in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways.

L.37: Turn my eyes away from looking at worthlessness; in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways give me life.

R.37: Keep me from looking at things that are worthless. Keep me alive as I follow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways.

decisions.choice: worthlessness: what is empty and false
decisions.reason: The word (shaw') is emptiness, what has no substance or is false; it is used of idols (31:7) and of lies (12:3).

decisions.choice: give me life: keep me alive, renew my life
as I walk in (B); as I follow (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how life and God's ways go together.

records.gloss: Fulfill to your servant your saying, which [is] for [the] fear of you.
pieces: Make good {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, so that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will be feared.

L.38: Fulfill to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying, which [is] for the fear of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.38: Do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} promised me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, so that people will stand in awe of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.reason: The verb (heqim) is to make a word stand, to carry out what was promised.

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often his promise
which is for the fear of you: so that you are feared
alternatives: which is for those who fear you
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean that keeping the promise leads people to revere God (as 130:4), or that the promise was made to those who fear him.
A promise is in view here, so Balanced and Readable say "promise" (see 119:11).

records.source: הַעֲבֵ֣ר חֶ֭רְפָּתִי אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָגֹ֑רְתִּי כִּ֖י מִשְׁפָּטֶ֣יךָ טוֹבִֽים׃
records.gloss: Take away my disgrace, which I dread, for your judgments [are] good.
pieces: Turn aside the scorn I fear so much, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings are good.

L.39: Take away my disgrace, which I dread, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments [are] good.

R.39: Take away the shame that I am afraid of. Your decisions are good.

decisions.reason: The word (cherpah) is the scorn and insults of others, as in verse 22.

decisions.choice: judgments: God's rulings, his decisions about what is right
decisions.reason: As in 119:7.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for the request
decisions.reason: Because God's rulings are good, the psalmist can ask him to take away the scorn that those rulings do not deserve.

records.gloss: Look, I long for your precepts; in your righteousness give me life.
pieces: See how I long for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts! Keep me alive in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.

L.40: Look, I long for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts; in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness give me life.

R.40: You can see how much I long for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions. You are righteous, so keep me alive.

decisions.choice: precepts: the charges God has laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:4.

decisions.choice: righteousness: God's doing what is right
decisions.reason: God's righteousness (tsedaqah) is his doing what is right, which includes keeping faith with those who trust him and rescuing them (31:2).

decisions.choice: give me life: keep me alive, renew my life

decisions.reason: Readable says how God's righteousness is the ground of the request.

records.gloss: And let come to me your loyal loves, YHWH, your salvation according to your saying.
pieces: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love reach me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rescue, as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise assured me.

L.41: And let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love come to me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying.

R.41: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love. Save me, just as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise said.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter waw, the sixth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1). Hebrew has few words that begin with waw, so every verse begins with the word "and" (waw).
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: loyal loves: many acts of loyal love
decisions.reason: The word is plural, for the many ways God shows his loyal love; it is rendered in the singular.

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often his promise

decisions.reason: The "and" that opens every verse of this stanza is there for the alphabet pattern; Balanced and Readable leave it out where it adds nothing.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.gloss: And I will answer [the one] taunting me a word, for I trust in your word.
pieces: Then I will have a reply for the one who mocks me, because I rely on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

L.42: And I will answer the one who taunts me a word, for I trust in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

R.42: Then I can answer people who make fun of me, because I trust {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

decisions.reason: The verse follows from the request in verse 41: once God has rescued him, the psalmist will have an answer.
The verb (charaf) is to heap scorn on someone; the noun in verse 39 comes from it.
As in 119:9.
The first "word" is the reply the psalmist will give; the second is God's word. The play on the two is lost in Balanced and Readable.

records.source: וְֽאַל־תַּצֵּ֬ל מִפִּ֣י דְבַר־אֱמֶ֣ת עַד־מְאֹ֑ד כִּ֖י לְמִשְׁפָּטֶ֣ךָ יִחָֽלְתִּי׃
records.gloss: And do not take from my mouth a word of truth up to muchness, for for your judgments I have waited.
pieces: Do not take the word of truth wholly from my mouth, for I have waited in hope for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings.

L.43: And do not take the word of truth utterly out of my mouth, for I have waited for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments.

R.43: Do not stop me from speaking {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} true word, because I am hoping in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions.

decisions.choice: the word of truth: God's true word
decisions.reason: The phrase may be God's word, which is true, or any true word the psalmist would speak; in this stanza it is what he speaks before others (verses 42, 46).
As in 119:8.
The verb (yichel) is to wait in hope. It comes again in verses 49, 74 and 81.

decisions.choice: judgments: God's rulings, his decisions about what is right
decisions.reason: As in 119:7.
Readable takes the first sense (m1).

records.gloss: And I will keep your instruction continually, forever and ever.
pieces: I will keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction always, for all time to come.

L.44: And I will keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction continually, forever and ever.

R.44: I will obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching every day, forever and ever.

decisions.reason: As in 119:1.

decisions.choice: forever and ever: for all time
decisions.reason: Two words for lasting time are put together for emphasis (9:6; 45:18).

records.gloss: And I will walk about in the broad [place], for your precepts I have sought.
pieces: I will walk where there is room and freedom, because I have searched for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

L.45: And I will walk about in a wide place, for I have sought {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

R.45: I will walk around free, because I have looked hard for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions.

decisions.reason: A broad place is the opposite of being hemmed in by enemies and trouble (18:20; 31:9).
As in 119:2.

decisions.choice: precepts: the charges God has laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:4.
Balanced and Readable say what the picture means.

records.source: וַאֲדַבְּרָ֣ה בְ֭עֵדֹתֶיךָ נֶ֥גֶד מְלָכִ֗ים וְלֹ֣א אֵבֽוֹשׁ׃
records.gloss: And I will speak of your testimonies before kings, and I will not be ashamed.
pieces: I will talk about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees in front of kings and not be put to shame.

L.46: And I will speak of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies before kings, and I will not be put to shame.

R.46: I will tell kings about what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared, and I will not be ashamed.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
decisions.reason: As in 119:2.
As in 119:6.

records.gloss: And I will delight myself in your commands, which I love.
pieces: I will find my joy in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, because I love them.

L.47: And I will delight in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, which I love.

R.47: I enjoy {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, because I love them.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: As in 119:6.

records.source: וְאֶשָּֽׂא־כַפַּ֗י אֶֽל־מִ֭צְוֺתֶיךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָהָ֗בְתִּי וְאָשִׂ֥יחָה בְחֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And I will lift up my palms to your commands, which I love, and I will meditate on your statutes.
pieces: I will raise my hands toward {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, which I love, and I will ponder {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

L.48: And I will lift up my palms to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, which I love, and I will meditate on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

R.48: I will lift my hands to honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, because I love them. And I will think deeply about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.choice: lift up my palms: a gesture of prayer and reverence
decisions.reason: Lifting the hands was the posture of prayer (28:2; 141:2). Here it shows reverence for God's commands, which come from him.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: As in 119:6.

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.
Readable says what the gesture means.

records.gloss: Remember [the] word to your servant, on which you have made me hope.
pieces: Keep in mind the word {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made me hope in it.

L.49: Remember the word to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, on which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made me hope.

R.49: Remember the word {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant. You gave me hope through it.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter zayin, the seventh letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1). Three of them (verses 49, 52, 55) begin with the verb "remember".

decisions.choice: remember: keep in mind and act on
decisions.reason: When God remembers (zakar), he acts on what he has said (Genesis 8:1; Exodus 2:24).
As in 119:9.
The verb is the one in verse 43, here in a form that means "cause to hope".

records.source: זֹ֣את נֶחָמָתִ֣י בְעָנְיִ֑י כִּ֖י אִמְרָתְךָ֣ חִיָּֽתְנִי׃
records.gloss: This [is] my comfort in my affliction, that your saying has given me life.
pieces: Here is my comfort when I am brought low: {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise has kept me alive.

L.50: This [is] my comfort in my affliction, that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying has given me life.

R.50: When I am suffering, I find comfort in this: {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise keeps me alive.

decisions.reason: The word ('oni) is hardship and humiliation, from the verb used in verses 67, 71 and 75.

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often his promise
give me life: keep me alive, renew my life

records.source: זֵ֭דִים הֱלִיצֻ֣נִי עַד־מְאֹ֑ד מִ֝תּֽוֹרָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א נָטִֽיתִי׃
records.gloss: [The] arrogant have mocked me up to muchness; from your instruction I have not turned aside.
pieces: The proud have heaped scorn on me without limit, yet I have not swerved from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

L.51: The arrogant have mocked me utterly; from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction I have not turned aside.

R.51: Proud people laugh at me without mercy, but I have not turned away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.reason: The verb (helits) is related to the word for the mocker in 1:1.
As in 119:8.
As in 119:1.

records.gloss: I have remembered your judgments from of old, YHWH, and I have comforted myself.
pieces: I call to mind {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings from long ago, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and I find comfort.

L.52: I remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments from of old, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and I take comfort.

R.52: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I remember the decisions {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made long ago, and they comfort me.

decisions.choice: judgments: God's rulings, his decisions about what is right
decisions.reason: As in 119:7.

decisions.choice: from of old: given long ago
decisions.reason: The word ('olam) is time beyond memory. God's rulings were given long ago and have stood ever since.
The verb (hitnachem) is to find comfort for oneself.

records.gloss: Burning rage has seized me because of [the] wicked, [who] forsake your instruction.
pieces: Because of the wicked, who have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction, a hot anger takes hold of me.

L.53: Burning anger has seized me because of the wicked, who forsake {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

R.53: I am filled with anger because of wicked people who turn their backs on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.reason: The word (zal'afah) is a burning heat, used of the scorching wind in 11:6. Here it is the psalmist's anger, or horror, at people who abandon God's instruction.
The verb ('azav) is the one in verse 8.
As in 119:1.

records.gloss: Songs have been to me your statutes in [the] house of my sojournings.
pieces: Your statutes have become my songs in every place where I live as a foreigner.

L.54: Songs {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes have been to me, in the house of my sojourning.

R.54: Wherever I live as a stranger, I sing about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.reason: The word (zemirot) is used of songs with instruments (95:2).

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.

decisions.choice: the house of my sojourning: wherever I live as a foreigner
decisions.reason: The psalmist calls himself a sojourner (verse 19); the house of his sojourning is his life on earth, lived as a foreigner who is only passing through (39:13).

decisions.choice: every place where I live as a foreigner (B); wherever I live as a stranger (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the phrase means.

records.source: זָ֘כַ֤רְתִּי בַלַּ֣יְלָה שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהוָ֑ה וָֽ֝אֶשְׁמְרָ֗ה תּוֹרָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: I have remembered in the night your name, YHWH, and I have kept your instruction.
pieces: Through the night I think of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and I hold to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

L.55: I remember in the night {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and I keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

R.55: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, at night I think about who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are, and I obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.choice: your name: God himself as he has made himself known
decisions.reason: A name stood for the person and what he had shown himself to be (5:12; 20:2).
As in 119:1.
The verb is past in form; it describes what the psalmist has done and still does, so it is rendered with the present, like "remember".
Readable says what the name stands for (m1).

records.gloss: This has been to me, that your precepts I have kept.
pieces: This has been my part in life: I have held to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

L.56: This has been mine: that I have kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

R.56: This is how I have lived: I have obeyed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions.

decisions.choice: this has been mine: this is what I have
alternatives: this has happened to me because I kept your precepts
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short and can be read two ways: keeping God's precepts is what the psalmist has as his own (as "my portion" in verse 57), or the comfort of verses 52-55 came to him because he kept them.

decisions.choice: precepts: the charges God has laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:4.
As in 119:2.

records.gloss: My portion [is] YHWH; I have said to keep your words.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is my share in life; I have said that I will hold to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words.

L.57: My portion [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; I have said [that I would] keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words.

R.57: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is all I need. I have promised to obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter heth, the eighth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1).

decisions.choice: my portion: my share, what I have
decisions.reason: The tribe of Levi received no land, for the LORD was its portion (Numbers 18:20). The psalmist says the same of himself (16:5; 73:26).

alternatives: My portion, LORD, I have said, is to keep your words
decisions.reason: The name may be the subject ("the LORD is my portion") or a call to God ("my portion, LORD, ..."). The psalm otherwise speaks to God, but the first reading is the plainer.

decisions.choice: I have said: I have promised
decisions.reason: To say that one will do something is to promise it.
As in 119:9; here the word is plural.
Readable says what the picture means.

records.gloss: I have entreated your face with all [the] heart; be gracious to me according to your saying.
pieces: With my whole heart I have pleaded for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} favor; show me kindness, just as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise said.

L.58: I have entreated {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face with all [the] heart; be gracious to me according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying.

R.58: I have begged {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with all my heart to be kind to me. Show me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kindness, just as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise said.

decisions.choice: entreat your face: plead for your favor
decisions.reason: The phrase (chillah panim) is to soften someone's face, to seek favor from a ruler or from God (Exodus 32:11).
The verb (chanan) is to show kindness that is not owed.

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often his promise

records.gloss: I have thought about my ways, and I have turned my feet to your testimonies.
pieces: I have thought hard about how I live, and turned my steps back to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees.

L.59: I have considered my ways, and I have turned my feet to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies.

R.59: I thought about the way I was living, and I turned back to do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared.

decisions.reason: Turning the feet is a picture of turning back to God, of repentance.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
decisions.reason: As in 119:2.
Balanced and Readable bring out that this is a turning back.

records.gloss: I have hurried and not delayed to keep your commands.
pieces: Quickly, without waiting, I set myself to keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

L.60: I have hurried and not delayed to keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

R.60: I hurry to obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands. I do not wait.

decisions.reason: The verb (hitmahmah) is to linger or hold back (Genesis 19:16).

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: As in 119:6.

records.source: חֶבְלֵ֣י רְשָׁעִ֣ים עִוְּדֻ֑נִי תּֽ֝וֹרָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א שָׁכָֽחְתִּי׃
records.gloss: [The] cords of [the] wicked have surrounded me; your instruction I have not forgotten.
pieces: The wicked have tangled me in their ropes, but I have not forgotten {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

L.61: The ropes of the wicked have wrapped around me; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction I have not forgotten.

R.61: Wicked people have tried to trap me, but I have not forgotten {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.reason: The word (chevel) is a rope, often of a hunter's snare (18:6; 140:6). It can also mean a band of people.
The verb ('iwwed) is rare; it seems to mean to surround or bind round.
As in 119:1.

alternatives: the ropes of the wicked have wrapped around me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of the snare means.

records.source: חֲצֽוֹת־לַ֗יְלָה אָ֭קוּם לְהוֹד֣וֹת לָ֑ךְ עַ֝֗ל מִשְׁפְּטֵ֥י צִדְקֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: [At the] middle of [the] night I rise to give thanks to you for [the] judgments of your righteousness.
pieces: In the middle of the night I get up to thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteous rulings.

L.62: At the middle of the night I rise to give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for the judgments of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.

R.62: In the middle of the night I get up to thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions are right.

decisions.reason: As in 119:7.

decisions.choice: judgments: God's rulings, his decisions about what is right
decisions.reason: As in 119:7.
As in 119:7.

records.source: חָבֵ֣ר אָ֭נִי לְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְרֵא֑וּךָ וּ֝לְשֹׁמְרֵ֗י פִּקּוּדֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: A companion I [am] of all who fear you, and of those keeping your precepts.
pieces: I stand with all who fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, with everyone who holds to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

L.63: A companion I [am] of all who fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and of those who keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

R.63: I am a friend of everyone who honors {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and obeys {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions.

decisions.choice: companion: one who is joined to others
decisions.reason: The word (chaver) is a companion or partner, someone bound to others in a shared life.
To fear God is to honor him with awe and to obey him (34:10).

decisions.choice: precepts: the charges God has laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:4.
Readable says "honor", since "fear" alone can sound like terror (m2).

records.source: חַסְדְּךָ֣ יְ֭הוָה מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֗רֶץ חֻקֶּ֥יךָ לַמְּדֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: [Of] your loyal love, YHWH, is full the earth; teach me your statutes.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love fills all the earth; teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

L.64: [With] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the earth is full; teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

R.64: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love is everywhere on earth. Teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.choice: the earth is full of his loyal love
decisions.reason: Psalm 33:5 says the same. The stanza ends where it began, with the LORD who fills all things and is the psalmist's portion.

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.gloss: Good you have done with your servant, YHWH, according to your word.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have treated {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant well, just as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word said.

L.65: Good {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

R.65: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been good to me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, just as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word said.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter teth, the ninth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1). Five of them (verses 65, 66, 68, 71, 72) begin with the word "good" (tov), the theme of the stanza.
As in 119:9.

records.source: ט֤וּב טַ֣עַם וָדַ֣עַת לַמְּדֵ֑נִי כִּ֖י בְמִצְוֺתֶ֣יךָ הֶאֱמָֽנְתִּי׃
records.gloss: Goodness of discernment and knowledge teach me, for in your commands I have believed.
pieces: Train me in good sense and knowledge, for I rely on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

L.66: Good discernment and knowledge teach me, for in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands I have trusted.

R.66: Teach me to know what is right and to make wise choices, because I trust {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

decisions.reason: The word (ta'am) is taste, and so the ability to tell good from bad (1 Samuel 25:33).
The verb (he'emin) is to hold something as firm and reliable and to lean on it.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: As in 119:6.

records.source: טֶ֣רֶם אֶ֭עֱנֶה אֲנִ֣י שֹׁגֵ֑ג וְ֝עַתָּ֗ה אִמְרָתְךָ֥ שָׁמָֽרְתִּי׃
records.gloss: Before I was afflicted I was going astray, and now your saying I keep.
pieces: Until I was brought low, I kept wandering off; but now I hold to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

L.67: Before I was afflicted I was going astray, but now {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying I keep.

R.67: Before I suffered, I wandered away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. But now I obey what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said.

decisions.reason: The verb ('anah) is to be bowed down by hardship. Verses 71 and 75 say that God used it to teach the psalmist.

decisions.choice: going astray: straying, often without knowing
decisions.reason: The verb (shagag) is used of wrong done by mistake (Leviticus 4:2).

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often his promise

decisions.reason: No promise is in view here, so Balanced says "word" and Readable "what you said" (see 119:11).
Readable says from whom the psalmist wandered.

records.gloss: Good [are] you, and doing good; teach me your statutes.
pieces: You are good, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring about good; teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

L.68: Good [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and doing good; teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

R.68: You are good, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do good things. Teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.choice: doing good: what God always does
decisions.reason: The participle describes what God does by nature: he is good and he does good.

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.

records.source: טָפְל֬וּ עָלַ֣י שֶׁ֣קֶר זֵדִ֑ים אֲ֝נִ֗י בְּכָל־לֵ֤ב׀אֱצֹּ֬ר פִּקּוּדֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: [The] arrogant have smeared on me falsehood; I with all [the] heart keep your precepts.
pieces: The proud have plastered lies all over me, but with my whole heart I hold to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

L.69: The arrogant have smeared lies on me; I, with all [the] heart, keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

R.69: Proud people tell lies to ruin my good name, but I obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions with all my heart.

decisions.choice: smeared lies on me: covered me with lies
decisions.reason: The verb (tafal) is to smear or plaster over (Job 13:4). Lies are spread over the psalmist to hide who he really is.

decisions.choice: precepts: the charges God has laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:4.

decisions.choice: tell lies to ruin my good name
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means.

records.source: טָפַ֣שׁ כַּחֵ֣לֶב לִבָּ֑ם אֲ֝נִ֗י תּוֹרָתְךָ֥ שִֽׁעֲשָֽׁעְתִּי׃
records.gloss: Their heart is unfeeling like fat; I, your instruction I delight in.
pieces: Their hearts are thick and dull as fat, but I delight in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

L.70: Their heart is gross like fat; as for me, I delight in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

R.70: Their hearts feel nothing, like a lump of fat. But {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching makes me glad.

decisions.choice: unfeeling like fat: dull, closed to God
decisions.reason: A heart covered in fat cannot feel or understand (Isaiah 6:10). The arrogant are set against the psalmist, who delights in God's instruction.
As in 119:1.

records.gloss: [It was] good for me that I was afflicted, so that I might learn your statutes.
pieces: It did me good to be brought low, so that I would learn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

L.71: It [was] good for me that I was afflicted, so that I might learn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

R.71: Suffering was good for me, so that I could learn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.reason: The psalmist does not call suffering good in itself, but says God used it to bring him back to his ways (verse 67; Deuteronomy 8:2-3).

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.

records.gloss: Better to me [is the] instruction of your mouth than thousands of gold and silver.
pieces: The instruction {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken is worth more to me than gold and silver by the thousand.

L.72: Better to me [is] the instruction of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mouth than thousands of gold and silver.

R.72: What {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach me is worth more to me than a fortune in gold and silver.

decisions.reason: Hebrew says "good ... more than" to mean "better than". The stanza's word "good" (tov) opens this verse too.
As in 119:1.

decisions.choice: thousands of gold and silver: great wealth
decisions.reason: The phrase means thousands of pieces (weights) of gold and silver (19:11).
Readable says what the amount means.

records.source: יָדֶ֣יךָ עָ֭שׂוּנִי וַֽיְכוֹנְנ֑וּנִי הֲ֝בִינֵ֗נִי וְאֶלְמְדָ֥ה מִצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Your hands made me and established me; give me understanding, and I will learn your commands.
pieces: Your hands made me and shaped me; give me insight, so that I can learn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

L.73: Your hands made me and established me; give me understanding, that I may learn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

R.73: You made me with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hands and formed me. Help me understand, so that I can learn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter yod, the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1). The first word, "your hands", begins with it.
The verb (konen) is to set up firmly; of a person, to fashion and make firm (Deuteronomy 32:6).
Job 10:8 uses the same picture: the one who made the psalmist can also teach him.

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: As in 119:6.

records.source: יְ֭רֵאֶיךָ יִרְא֣וּנִי וְיִשְׂמָ֑חוּ כִּ֖י לִדְבָרְךָ֣ יִחָֽלְתִּי׃
records.gloss: Those fearing you will see me and rejoice, for for your word I have waited.
pieces: Those who fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will be glad when they see me, for I have set my hope on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

L.74: Those who fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will see me and rejoice, for I have waited for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

R.74: People who honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will be happy when they see me, because I counted on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

decisions.choice: will see and rejoice: or a wish, may they see
alternatives: may those who fear you see me and rejoice
decisions.reason: The verbs may state what will happen or express a wish.
As in 119:9.

records.source: יָדַ֣עְתִּי יְ֭הוָה כִּי־צֶ֣דֶק מִשְׁפָּטֶ֑יךָ וֶ֝אֱמוּנָ֗ה עִנִּיתָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: I know, YHWH, that righteousness [are] your judgments, and [in] faithfulness you have afflicted me.
pieces: I know, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings are just, and that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought me low because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are faithful.

L.75: I know, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments [are] righteousness, and [in] faithfulness {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have afflicted me.

R.75: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I know that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions are right. You made me suffer because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are faithful to me.

decisions.choice: judgments: God's rulings, his decisions about what is right
decisions.reason: As in 119:7.

decisions.choice: in faithfulness you have afflicted me
decisions.reason: The hardship the psalmist went through was not a sign that God had left him but part of God's faithful care, as a father disciplines a son (Deuteronomy 8:5).
Readable says to whom God is faithful.

records.gloss: Let, please, your loyal love be to comfort me, according to your saying to your servant.
pieces: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love comfort me, I pray, as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant said.

L.76: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, please, be for my comfort, according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.

R.76: Please let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love comfort me, just as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise to me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, said.

decisions.reason: The verb (nicham) is related to the one in verses 52 and 82.

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often his promise

decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.gloss: Let your compassions come to me, that I may live, for your instruction [is] my delight.
pieces: Send {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} tender mercy to me so that I may live; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction is what I delight in.

L.77: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} compassion come to me, that I may live, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction [is] my delight.

R.77: Be kind and gentle with me so that I may live. Your teaching gives me joy.

decisions.reason: The word (rachamim) is related to the word for the womb: the tender love of a parent (103:13). It is plural, for many acts of mercy.
As in 119:1.

decisions.choice: be kind and gentle with me
alternatives: let your compassion come to me
decisions.reason: Readable says what God's compassion coming means.

records.source: יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ זֵ֭דִים כִּי־שֶׁ֣קֶר עִוְּת֑וּנִי אֲ֝נִ֗י אָשִׂ֥יחַ בְּפִקּוּדֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Let [the] arrogant be put to shame, for [with] falsehood they have wronged me; I, I will meditate on your precepts.
pieces: Let the proud be disgraced, for they have twisted the truth to harm me; but I will ponder {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

L.78: Let the arrogant be put to shame, for with lies they have wronged me; as for me, I will meditate on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

R.78: Let proud people be put to shame, because they told lies to hurt me. But I will think deeply about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions.

decisions.reason: The verb ('iwwet) is to bend or falsify; they have twisted the truth to bring the psalmist down (Job 8:3; Lamentations 3:36).

decisions.choice: precepts: the charges God has laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:4.

records.gloss: Let those fearing you turn to me, and those knowing your testimonies.
pieces: Let those who fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come back to me, those who know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees.

L.79: Let those who fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn to me, and those who know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies.

R.79: Let the people who honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come back to me, the ones who know what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared.

decisions.choice: and those who know: the form to be read
alternatives: so that they may know your testimonies
decisions.reason: The words follow the form to be read. The written form seems to read "and they will know", making the second line the purpose of the first; the sense is close.

decisions.choice: turn to me: come back to me
decisions.reason: The verb (shuv) is to turn or return; those who fear God may have drawn back while the psalmist suffered.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
decisions.reason: As in 119:2.

records.source: יְהִֽי־לִבִּ֣י תָמִ֣ים בְּחֻקֶּ֑יךָ לְ֝מַ֗עַן לֹ֣א אֵבֽוֹשׁ׃
records.gloss: Let my heart be blameless in your statutes, so that I may not be ashamed.
pieces: Let my heart be whole in keeping {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes, so that I will not be disgraced.

L.80: May my heart be blameless in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes, so that I may not be put to shame.

R.80: Help me obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws with all my heart, so that I will not be ashamed.

decisions.reason: As in 119:1.

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.
As in 119:6.

decisions.choice: help me obey ... with all my heart
decisions.reason: Readable turns the wish into a prayer and says what a whole heart means.

records.gloss: My soul is spent for your salvation; for your word I have waited.
pieces: I am worn out with longing for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rescue; I have set my hope on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

L.81: My soul faints for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation; for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word I have waited.

R.81: I long so much for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to save me that I have no strength left. Still, I keep hoping in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter kaph, the eleventh letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1). Verses 81-87 are the darkest part of the psalm so far.
The verb (kalah) is to come to an end, to be used up. It comes again in verse 82, and in verse 87 of the enemies who almost made an end of the psalmist.
As in 119:9.
As in the earlier psalms, Literal keeps "soul" (nefesh) and Balanced and Readable say what it means here, the whole person.

records.source: כָּל֣וּ עֵ֭ינַי לְאִמְרָתֶ֑ךָ לֵ֝אמֹ֗ר מָתַ֥י תְּֽנַחֲמֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: My eyes are spent for your saying, saying: when will you comfort me?
pieces: My eyes grow dim as I watch for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise; I keep asking when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will comfort me.

L.82: My eyes fail for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying, as I say: when will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} comfort me?

R.82: My eyes are tired from watching for what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} promised. I keep asking when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will comfort me.

decisions.choice: my eyes fail: I have watched until I can watch no longer
decisions.reason: Eyes that fail are worn out with looking for help that does not come (69:4).

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often his promise

decisions.reason: The question is the psalmist's own; as elsewhere, his own words are not put in quotation marks.

records.source: כִּֽי־הָ֭יִיתִי כְּנֹ֣אד בְּקִיט֑וֹר חֻ֝קֶּ֗יךָ לֹ֣א שָׁכָֽחְתִּי׃
records.gloss: For I have become like a wineskin in smoke; your statutes I have not forgotten.
pieces: I am like a skin bottle dried and cracked in the smoke, yet {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes have not slipped my mind.

L.83: For I have become like a wineskin in smoke; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes I have not forgotten.

R.83: I am dried up and useless, like an old leather bottle hanging in smoke. But I have not forgotten {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.choice: a wineskin in smoke: shriveled and useless
decisions.reason: Wine and water were kept in bottles made of animal skin. One hung in the smoke of a fire, in a house without a chimney, would dry out, blacken and crack.
The word (ki) may give the reason for the cry in verse 82, or mean "though", leading to the second line.

decisions.choice: statutes: rules that are fixed and laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:5.
Readable says what the picture means (m1).

records.source: כַּמָּ֥ה יְמֵֽי־עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ מָתַ֬י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בְרֹדְפַ֣י מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
records.gloss: How many [are the] days of your servant? When will you do on [those] pursuing me judgment?
pieces: How many days does {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant have left? When will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge those who hunt me down?

L.84: How many [are] the days of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant? When will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} execute judgment on those who pursue me?

R.84: I do not have long to live. When will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring the people who chase me to justice?

decisions.choice: how many are the days of your servant: my life is short
decisions.reason: The question means that the psalmist's life is short and he cannot wait long for God to act (39:5; 89:48).

Here the word (mishpat) is not one of the psalm's words for God's law but its usual sense: God's verdict on those who wrong the psalmist. This is one of the few verses of the psalm with none of the eight words.
The verb (radaf) is to chase someone down, as in verse 86.

decisions.choice: I do not have long to live
alternatives: how many are the days of your servant?
decisions.reason: Readable says what the question means (m1).

records.source: כָּֽרוּ־לִ֣י זֵדִ֣ים שִׁיח֑וֹת אֲ֝שֶׁ֗ר לֹ֣א כְתוֹרָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: [The] arrogant have dug for me pits, which [are] not according to your instruction.
pieces: The proud have dug pits to catch me, people who do not live by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

L.85: The arrogant have dug pits for me, which [is] not according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

R.85: Proud people have dug holes to trap me. They do not follow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.reason: Hunters dug pits and covered them over to trap animals (7:16; 57:7).

decisions.choice: which: the people, or what they do
decisions.reason: "Which" may refer to the arrogant, who do not live by God's instruction, or to their digging of pits, which his instruction forbids. The sense is the same.
As in 119:1.

records.gloss: All your commands [are] faithfulness; [with] falsehood they have pursued me; help me!
pieces: All {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands can be trusted; people hunt me down with lies. Help me!

L.86: All {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands [are] faithfulness; with falsehood they have pursued me; help me!

R.86: All {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands are true and can be trusted. People are chasing me with lies. Help me!

decisions.choice: commands: what God has told his people to do
decisions.reason: As in 119:6.
As in 119:30: God's commands are steady and true.

decisions.choice: with falsehood: with lies, without cause
decisions.reason: The word (sheqer) is the one in verse 29; the psalmist is hunted by lies and for no reason.

records.source: כִּ֭מְעַט כִּלּ֣וּנִי בָאָ֑רֶץ וַ֝אֲנִ֗י לֹא־עָזַ֥בְתִּי פִקֻּודֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Almost they have made an end of me on the earth, but I, I have not forsaken your precepts.
pieces: They came close to finishing me off in the land, yet I have not let go of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

L.87: Almost they have made an end of me on the earth, but as for me, I have not forsaken {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

R.87: They almost killed me, but I have not turned away from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions.

decisions.reason: The verb is the one in verses 81-82 (kalah), here "finish off".
The word ('erets) can mean the whole earth or the land.

decisions.choice: precepts: the charges God has laid down
decisions.reason: As in 119:4.

records.gloss: According to your loyal love give me life, and I will keep [the] testimony of your mouth.
pieces: Keep me alive in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, and I will hold to the decree {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken.

L.88: According to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love give me life, and I will keep the testimony of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mouth.

R.88: Keep me alive because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love, and I will obey what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared.

decisions.choice: give me life: keep me alive, renew my life
testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
decisions.reason: As in 119:2; here the word is singular ('edut).
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.gloss: Forever, YHWH, your word [is] standing firm in the heavens.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word lasts forever; it is fixed in place in the heavens.

L.89: Forever, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word [is] standing firm in the heavens.

R.89: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word lasts forever. It is set firmly in heaven, where nothing can shake it.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter lamed, the twelfth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1).

decisions.choice: standing firm: set in place, stationed
decisions.reason: The verb (nitsav) is used of something set up to stand, like a pillar or a guard at his post. God's word is as fixed as the heavens where he reigns (verses 90-91).
The word (davar) is the broadest of the psalm's eight terms for what God has made known: anything he has spoken, whether command or promise.
Readable spells out what it means for the word to stand firm in heaven.

records.source: לְדֹ֣ר וָ֭דֹר אֱמֽוּנָתֶ֑ךָ כּוֹנַ֥נְתָּ אֶ֝֗רֶץ וַֽתַּעֲמֹֽד׃
records.gloss: To generation and generation [is] your faithfulness; you established [the] earth, and it stands.
pieces: Your faithfulness lasts from one generation to the next; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set the earth in its place, and it remains.

L.90: To generation and generation [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} established the earth, and it stands.

R.90: You stay faithful to people in every age. You made the earth firm, and it is still standing.
