decisions.choice: to generation and generation: through all generations
decisions.reason: The doubled word means every generation in turn, without end.

decisions.choice: it stands: it endures, it stays in place
decisions.reason: The verb ('amad) is to stand. The earth God set up has not fallen; verse 91 uses the same verb of all creation.

records.source: לְֽ֭מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ עָמְד֣וּ הַיּ֑וֹם כִּ֖י הַכֹּ֣ל עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: By your judgments they stand this day, for everything [are] your servants.
pieces: They stand today by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings, since all things are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants.

L.91: By {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments they stand this day, for all things [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants.

R.91: Heaven and earth are still here today because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions. Everything there is serves {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: they: the heavens and the earth
alternatives: they stand (ready) today for your rulings
decisions.reason: "They" are most likely the heavens and the earth of verses 89-90, which stand because God has ruled that they should (compare Jeremiah 33:25). The words can also mean that they stand ready, like servants, waiting for his rulings.
The word (mishpatim) is the decision of a judge. Here it is what God has ruled to be right, which he also carries out. Here they are the rulings by which God orders creation.
As throughout the psalm, Literal keeps "judgments", Balanced says "rulings" and Readable "decisions", so that the sense of a judge's verdict is not lost.
Everything God made does his will; nothing in creation is his rival (104:4).
Readable names what "they" refers to (m1).

records.source: לוּלֵ֣י ת֭וֹרָתְךָ שַׁעֲשֻׁעָ֑י אָ֝֗ז אָבַ֥דְתִּי בְעָנְיִֽי׃
records.gloss: If not your instruction [had been] my delight, then I [would have] perished in my affliction.
pieces: Had I not taken delight in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction, I would have died in my trouble.

L.92: If {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction [had] not [been] my delight, then I [would have] perished in my affliction.

R.92: If I had not loved {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching so much, my suffering would have killed me.

decisions.reason: The word (torah) is teaching or direction, from a verb meaning to point the way. In this psalm it is God's whole teaching for his people, not only a set of rules.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "teaching" for torah.

decisions.choice: delight: joy, what one plays and delights in
decisions.reason: The word (sha'ashu'im) is plural, "delights": the deepest pleasure (verses 24, 77, 143, 174).
The word ('oni) is misery and humiliation, often at the hands of others.

records.source: לְ֭עוֹלָם לֹא־אֶשְׁכַּ֣ח פִּקּוּדֶ֑יךָ כִּ֥י בָ֝֗ם חִיִּיתָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Forever I will not forget your precepts, for by them you have given me life.
pieces: Never will I forget {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have used them to give me life.

L.93: Forever I will not forget {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts, for by them {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given me life.

R.93: I will always remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have used them to keep me alive.

decisions.reason: "Forever I will not forget" is a strong way of saying "I will never forget".
The word (piqqudim) comes from a verb meaning to appoint or put in charge. It occurs only in the Psalms, for the particular charges God has given his people.
Readable uses a plainer word, as throughout the psalm.

decisions.choice: give me life: keep me alive, renew my life

records.gloss: To you I [belong]; save me, for your precepts I have sought.
pieces: I belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; save me, for I have searched out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

L.94: Yours [am] I; save me, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts I have sought.

R.94: I am {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}, so save me! I have tried hard to follow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions.

decisions.choice: to you I belong: I am yours
decisions.reason: The words "to you, I" mean that the psalmist belongs to God, which is the ground of his plea.
The verb (darash) is to seek, inquire, and so to give one's attention and care to something (verses 2, 10, 45, 155).
Readable says what seeking God's precepts leads to.

records.source: לִ֤י קִוּ֣וּ רְשָׁעִ֣ים לְאַבְּדֵ֑נִי עֵ֝דֹתֶ֗יךָ אֶתְבּוֹנָֽן׃
records.gloss: For me [the] wicked have waited to destroy me; your testimonies I consider.
pieces: The wicked lie in wait to destroy me, but I keep my mind on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees.

L.95: For me [the] wicked have waited to destroy me; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies I consider.

R.95: Wicked people are waiting for a chance to kill me. But I think hard about what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared.

decisions.reason: The verb (qivvah) is to wait or hope; here the wicked wait for their chance.
The verb (hitbonen) is to think something through until one understands it.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
decisions.reason: The word ('edot) is related to the verb "testify, warn". It is what God has solemnly declared and bound his people to; the tablets of the covenant are called "the testimony" (Exodus 25:16).
As throughout the psalm, Literal keeps "testimonies", which no longer says much to most readers; Balanced says "decrees" and Readable "what you have declared".
The Hebrew sets the two lines side by side; Balanced and Readable show the contrast.

records.source: לְֽכָל תִּ֭כְלָה רָאִ֣יתִי קֵ֑ץ רְחָבָ֖ה מִצְוָתְךָ֣ מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: To all perfection I have seen an end; broad [is] your command exceedingly.
pieces: I have seen that every perfect thing has its limit, but {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} command reaches wide beyond measure.

L.96: To all perfection I have seen an end; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} command [is] exceedingly broad.

R.96: I have seen that even the best things in this world come to an end. But {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} command is wider than anything.

decisions.reason: The word (tikhlah) occurs only here; it comes from a verb meaning to be complete or finished. Even the most complete things have an end.
A broad command is one whose reach has no end, unlike every perfect thing in the first line.
The word (mitsvah) comes from the verb "command" (tsivvah): what God has told his people to do. Here it is singular, God's command as a whole.
Balanced and Readable show the contrast between the two lines.

records.gloss: How I love your instruction! All the day it [is] my meditation.
pieces: How I love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction! I turn it over in my mind all day long.

L.97: How I love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction! All the day it [is] my meditation.

R.97: I love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching so much! I think about it all day.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter mem, the thirteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1).

decisions.choice: meditation: what one turns over in the mind
decisions.reason: The word (sichah) is thinking something over, perhaps half aloud (verse 99).

records.source: מֵ֭אֹ֣יְבַי תְּחַכְּמֵ֣נִי מִצְוֺתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם הִיא־לִֽי׃
records.gloss: More than my enemies your commands make me wise, for forever it [is] with me.
pieces: Through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands I grow wiser than my enemies, since they are mine forever.

L.98: More than my enemies {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands make me wise, for forever it [is] with me.

R.98: Because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands, I am wiser than my enemies. They are always with me.

decisions.reason: The noun is plural, but the verb and the pronoun "it" are singular: the commands are taken together as one body of teaching.
Balanced and Readable say "they" to agree with "commands" (m1).

records.source: מִכָּל־מְלַמְּדַ֥י הִשְׂכַּ֑לְתִּי כִּ֥י עֵ֝דְוֺתֶ֗יךָ שִׂ֣יחָה לִֽֿי׃
records.gloss: More than all my teachers I have insight, for your testimonies [are] a meditation to me.
pieces: I see more deeply than all my teachers, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees fill my thoughts.

L.99: More than all my teachers I have insight, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies [are] my meditation.

R.99: I understand more than all my teachers, because I think about what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared.

decisions.reason: The verb (hiskil) is to have the kind of understanding that leads to wise action.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
wiser than teachers: the gift of God's word
decisions.reason: The claim in verses 98-100 is not pride in himself but praise for what God's word gives to one who takes it to heart.

records.gloss: More than [the] old I understand, for your precepts I have kept.
pieces: I understand more than the old, because I have kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

L.100: More than [the] elders I understand, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts I have kept.

R.100: I understand more than people who have lived a long time, because I have obeyed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions.

decisions.reason: The word (zeqenim) is the old, who were expected to be wise from long experience, and the elders who led the people.

records.source: מִכָּל־אֹ֣רַח רָ֭ע כָּלִ֣אתִי רַגְלָ֑י לְ֝מַ֗עַן אֶשְׁמֹ֥ר דְּבָרֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: From every evil path I have held back my feet, so that I may keep your word.
pieces: I have held my feet back from every wicked road, so that I may keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

L.101: From every evil path I have held back my feet, so that I may keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

R.101: I have stayed away from every evil way of life, so that I can do what {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word says.

decisions.choice: path and feet: the way one lives
decisions.reason: A path is a way of life, and the feet are the person who walks in it (verse 105).

records.gloss: From your judgments I have not turned aside, for you, you have taught me.
pieces: I have not strayed from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} have been my teacher.

L.102: From {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments I have not turned aside, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} have taught me.

R.102: I have kept to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} have taught me.

decisions.choice: you yourself: the pronoun is stressed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds "you" before the verb, which already includes it: it is God himself who has taught him.

records.gloss: How smooth to my palate are your sayings, more than honey to my mouth!
pieces: How sweet {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words taste to me, sweeter than honey on my tongue!

L.103: How smooth to my palate [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sayings, more than honey to my mouth!

R.103: What {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said tastes so good to me! It is sweeter than honey.

decisions.choice: are smooth: are pleasant, slip down easily
decisions.reason: The verb (nimlats) occurs only here; it seems to mean smooth or pleasant to the taste.

decisions.choice: sayings: plural verb with the noun
decisions.reason: The noun is written as if singular, but the verb is plural, so it is read as "your sayings".

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often a promise
decisions.reason: The word ('imrah) comes from the verb "say". In this psalm it is often what God has promised (verses 116, 154, 170), and sometimes simply what he has said. Here nothing is promised: it is God's words.

decisions.choice: word or promise (B); what you said or promised (R)
decisions.reason: As throughout the psalm, Literal keeps "saying"; Balanced says "promise" where a promise is in view and "word" where it is not, and Readable says "what you have said" or "what you promised".
Psalm 19:11 says the same of the LORD's judgments.

records.gloss: From your precepts I gain understanding; therefore I hate every path of falsehood.
pieces: Through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts I gain understanding, so I hate every road built on lies.

L.104: From {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts I gain understanding; therefore I hate every path of falsehood.

R.104: I learn wisdom from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions. That is why I hate every way of life that is based on lies.

decisions.choice: path of falsehood: a way of life built on lies
decisions.reason: "Falsehood" (sheqer) describes the path: a life that rests on what is untrue. Verse 128 repeats the line.

decisions.choice: every road built on lies (B); every way of life that is based on lies (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the phrase (m2), the same way here and in verse 128.

records.gloss: A lamp to my foot [is] your word, and a light to my path.
pieces: Your word is a lamp to guide my feet and a light for the road I travel.

L.105: A lamp to my foot [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word, and a light to my path.

R.105: Your word is like a lamp that shows me where to step. It is a light for the road I walk on.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter nun, the fourteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1).

decisions.choice: lamp and light: guidance in the dark
decisions.reason: A small oil lamp lit the next step on a dark road. God's word shows the way to go (Proverbs 6:23 says the same of a parent's command and teaching).

decisions.choice: to guide (B); shows me where to step (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the lamp does for the feet (m2).

records.gloss: I have sworn, and I have confirmed [it], to keep [the] judgments of your righteousness.
pieces: I have sworn an oath and I stand by it: I will keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteous rulings.

L.106: I have sworn, and I have confirmed [it], to keep the judgments of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.

R.106: I have made a solemn promise, and I will not go back on it. I will obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions, which are always right.

decisions.reason: The verb (qiyyem) is to make something stand, to confirm or carry out a promise.

decisions.choice: the judgments of your righteousness: your righteous judgments
decisions.reason: The phrase describes the judgments as righteous (also verses 160 and 164).

records.gloss: I have been afflicted very much; YHWH, give me life according to your word.
pieces: I am bowed down with trouble; {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, give me life as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word has said.

L.107: I have been afflicted very much; {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, give me life according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

R.107: I am suffering terribly. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, keep me alive, as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word says {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will.

decisions.choice: give me life: keep me alive, renew my life

decisions.reason: As in 119:89. Here it is what God has said he will do.
Readable makes clear that the word is a promise to be kept.

records.source: נִדְב֣וֹת פִּ֭י רְצֵה־נָ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וּֽמִשְׁפָּטֶ֥יךָ לַמְּדֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: [The] freewill offerings of my mouth accept, please, YHWH, and your judgments teach me.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please accept the praise I freely offer, and teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings.

L.108: The freewill offerings of my mouth accept, please, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments teach me.

R.108: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please accept the prayers and praise I gladly give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions.

decisions.choice: freewill offerings of my mouth: praise freely given
decisions.reason: A freewill offering was a sacrifice given by choice, not by duty (Leviticus 7:16). The psalmist offers words of prayer and praise in the same way (compare 50:14; Hosea 14).

decisions.choice: the praise I freely offer (B); the prayers and praise I gladly give you (R)
alternatives: the freewill offerings of my mouth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the offerings are (m1).

records.source: נַפְשִׁ֣י בְכַפִּ֣י תָמִ֑יד וְ֝תֽוֹרָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א שָׁכָֽחְתִּי׃
records.gloss: My soul [is] in my palm continually, but your instruction I have not forgotten.
pieces: Every day my life hangs in the balance, yet I do not forget {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

L.109: My soul [is] in my hand continually, but {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction I have not forgotten.

R.109: I am always in danger of losing my life. Still, I do not forget {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.choice: my soul in my hand: my life in constant danger
decisions.reason: To hold one's life in one's hand is to risk it (Judges 12:3; Job 13:14).

decisions.choice: my life hangs in the balance (B); in danger of losing my life (R)
alternatives: my life is in my hand
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the picture (m1).

records.source: נָתְנ֬וּ רְשָׁעִ֣ים פַּ֣ח לִ֑י וּ֝מִפִּקּוּדֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א תָעִֽיתִי׃
records.gloss: [The] wicked have set a trap for me, but from your precepts I have not strayed.
pieces: The wicked spread a trap to catch me, yet I have not wandered from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

L.110: [The] wicked have laid a trap for me, but from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts I have not strayed.

R.110: Wicked people try to trap me, but I have not stopped following {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions.

decisions.reason: The word (pach) is a trap for birds, a common picture for hidden danger (91:3; 124:7).

records.source: נָחַ֣לְתִּי עֵדְוֺתֶ֣יךָ לְעוֹלָ֑ם כִּֽי־שְׂשׂ֖וֹן לִבִּ֣י הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: I have inherited your testimonies forever, for [the] joy of my heart [are] they.
pieces: I have received {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees as my portion for all time; they make my heart glad.

L.111: I have inherited {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies forever, for the joy of my heart [are] they.

R.111: What {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared belongs to me forever, like land handed down in a family. It fills my heart with joy.

decisions.choice: inherited: received as a lasting possession
decisions.reason: Each family in Israel held its land as an inheritance that was not to be lost. The Levites had no land; the LORD himself was their inheritance (Numbers 18:20). The psalmist counts God's testimonies as his.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
like land handed down in a family
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of inheritance (m1).

records.source: נָטִ֣יתִי לִ֭בִּי לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת חֻקֶּ֗יךָ לְעוֹלָ֥ם עֵֽקֶב׃
records.gloss: I have inclined my heart to do your statutes forever, [to the] end.
pieces: I have turned my heart to carry out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes for all time, to the very end.

L.112: I have inclined my heart to do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes forever, to the end.

R.112: I have made up my mind to obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws for as long as I live.

decisions.choice: inclined my heart: set my mind and will
decisions.reason: To turn the heart toward something is to choose it with one's whole will (verse 36).

decisions.choice: statutes: what God has laid down
decisions.reason: The word (chuqqim) comes from a verb meaning to engrave or inscribe: what God has fixed in writing to stand.
Readable uses a plainer word, as throughout the psalm.
The word ('eqev) is the end or the outcome of something, and can mean a reward (19:12). Here it most likely means "to the end", strengthening "forever".

records.gloss: Half-hearted [people] I hate, but your instruction I love.
pieces: I hate people whose loyalty is divided, but I love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

L.113: [The] double-minded I hate, but {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction I love.

R.113: I hate people who cannot make up their minds whom to follow. But I love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter samekh, the fifteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1).

decisions.choice: the double-minded: people divided in their loyalty
decisions.reason: The word (se'afim) occurs only here. A related word is used in 1 Kings 18 of the people who went limping between the LORD and Baal.

records.gloss: My hiding place and my shield [are] you; for your word I wait.
pieces: In {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I find my hiding place and my shield; my hope is fixed on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

L.114: My hiding place and my shield [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word I wait.

R.114: You are where I hide, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} protect me like a shield. I trust {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word and wait for it.

decisions.choice: hiding place and shield: shelter and protection
decisions.reason: God is a place to hide from danger (32:7) and a shield against attack (3:4).
The verb (yichel) is to wait with hope and expectation (verses 43, 74, 81, 147).

records.gloss: Turn aside from me, evildoers, so that I may keep [the] commands of my God.
pieces: Get away from me, you evildoers! I mean to keep the commands my God has given.

L.115: Turn aside from me, evildoers, so that I may keep the commands of my God.

R.115: Stay away from me, you people who do evil! I want to obey my God's commands.

decisions.reason: Here the psalmist turns to speak to evildoers, and calls God "my God" ('Elohai), the only time the psalm uses that word for God; everywhere else it uses his name or speaks to him as "you".

decisions.choice: I mean to keep (B); I want to obey (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is a form that expresses resolve. Balanced and Readable state the psalmist's purpose as a resolve of his own.

records.gloss: Uphold me according to your saying, and I will live, and do not put me to shame from my hope.
pieces: Hold me up as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have promised, so that I may live; do not let my hope end in shame.

L.116: Uphold me according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying, and I will live, and do not put me to shame from my hope.

R.116: Hold me up, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} promised, so that I can live. Do not let me be disappointed because I hoped in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often a promise
decisions.reason: As in 119:103. Here it is a promise.

decisions.choice: do not shame me from my hope: do not let my hope fail
decisions.reason: To be put to shame is to be let down, publicly, by what one trusted (25:3).
Readable names the one in whom the psalmist hopes.

records.gloss: Support me, and I will be saved, and I will look to your statutes continually.
pieces: Hold me fast, and I will be safe; I will keep my eyes on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes always.

L.117: Support me, and I will be saved, and I will look to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes continually.

R.117: Hold on to me, and I will be safe. Then I will always pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.reason: The verb (sha'ah) is to look at something with attention and regard.

decisions.choice: statutes: what God has laid down

records.gloss: You reject all [who] stray from your statutes, for falsehood [is] their deceit.
pieces: You throw aside all who wander from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes, for their cunning is an empty lie.

L.118: You reject all who stray from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes, for falsehood [is] their deceit.

R.118: You turn away from everyone who stops obeying {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws. Their tricks are lies and will come to nothing.

decisions.reason: The verb (salah) is rare; it is used of the Lord throwing down the strong (Lamentations 1:15).

decisions.choice: statutes: what God has laid down
falsehood is their deceit: their cunning comes to nothing
decisions.reason: Their schemes are themselves a lie: they deceive, and they will fail. The ancient Greek translation reads "their thought" for "their deceit".
Readable spells out what it means for their deceit to be falsehood (m3).

records.source: סִגִ֗ים הִשְׁבַּ֥תָּ כָל־רִשְׁעֵי־אָ֑רֶץ לָ֝כֵ֗ן אָהַ֥בְתִּי עֵדֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: [As] dross you have removed all [the] wicked of [the] earth; therefore I love your testimonies.
pieces: All the wicked of the earth {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} throw away like dross; that is why I love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees.

L.119: [As] dross {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have removed all the wicked of the earth; therefore I love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies.

R.119: You throw away all the wicked people on earth, like the waste skimmed off when silver is made pure. That is why I love what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared.

decisions.reason: When silver was melted, the impurities rose and were skimmed off and thrown away (Isaiah 1:22, 25; Ezekiel 22:18).

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
the waste skimmed off when silver is made pure
decisions.reason: Readable explains what dross is (m1).

records.gloss: My flesh bristles from dread of you, and of your judgments I am afraid.
pieces: My skin crawls with dread of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings fill me with fear.

L.120: My flesh bristles from dread of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments I am afraid.

R.120: I shiver with fear when I think of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Your decisions make me afraid.

decisions.choice: bristles: shudders, the hair stands on end
decisions.reason: The verb (samar) is used of hair standing up in terror (Job 4:15).
As in 119:91. After verse 119 they are God's rulings as he carries them out against the wicked.

decisions.choice: dread of you: awe before God
decisions.reason: The psalmist loves God's word (verse 119) and also trembles before him; the two belong together.

records.gloss: I have done justice and righteousness; do not leave me to my oppressors.
pieces: I have done what is fair and just; do not give me up to those who oppress me.

L.121: I have done justice and righteousness; do not leave me to my oppressors.

R.121: I have done what is fair and right. Do not abandon me to people who are treating me cruelly.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter ayin, the sixteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1).

decisions.choice: justice and righteousness: what is fair and right
decisions.reason: The pair describes right dealing toward others (Genesis 18:19). Here "justice" (mishpat) is not one of the psalm's words for God's law.
The negative (bal) with the verb can be a plea or a statement of confidence; as a plea it fits the requests in verses 122-125.

records.gloss: Stand surety for your servant for good; let not [the] arrogant oppress me.
pieces: Pledge {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant's good; do not let the proud crush me.

L.122: Stand surety for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant for good; let not [the] arrogant oppress me.

R.122: Promise to take care of me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, and make things go well for me. Do not let proud people treat me cruelly.

decisions.choice: stand surety: pledge oneself for another
decisions.reason: A surety ('arav) took on another person's debt or danger as his own (Genesis 43:9; Proverbs 6:1). The psalmist asks God to stand behind him like that.
The psalmist speaks of himself as God's servant ('eved), one who belongs to God and serves him.

decisions.choice: the arrogant: proud people who scorn God
decisions.reason: The word (zedim) is used in this psalm for those who look down on God's word and on the psalmist (verses 21, 51, 69, 78, 85).

decisions.choice: a line without a word for God's law
decisions.reason: This is one of the few lines in the psalm that does not name God's word in any of its eight terms.

records.gloss: My eyes fail for your salvation, and for [the] saying of your righteousness.
pieces: My eyes grow weary as I watch for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation and for the righteous promise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made.

L.123: My eyes fail for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation, and for the saying of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.

R.123: My eyes are tired from looking for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to save me and to keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promise to do what is right.

decisions.choice: my eyes fail: I have watched until I am worn out
decisions.reason: Eyes that fail have looked so long for help that they give out (69:4; verse 82).

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often a promise
decisions.reason: As in 119:103. Here it is God's promise, described as righteous: a promise to set things right.
Readable turns "your salvation" into what God does.

records.gloss: Deal with your servant according to your loyal love, and your statutes teach me.
pieces: Treat {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love moves {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

L.124: Deal with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes teach me.

R.124: Treat me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love. Teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

decisions.choice: statutes: what God has laid down

records.gloss: Your servant [am] I; give me understanding, so that I may know your testimonies.
pieces: I am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant; make me understand, so that I come to know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees.

L.125: Your servant [am] I; give me understanding, so that I may know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies.

R.125: I am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant. Help me understand, so that I will know what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared.

decisions.reason: The psalmist speaks of himself as God's servant ('eved), one who belongs to God and serves him.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared

records.gloss: [It is] time to act for YHWH; they have broken your instruction.
pieces: The time has come for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to act, for people have broken {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

L.126: [It is] time to act for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; they have broken {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

R.126: Now is the time for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to do something! People have thrown away {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.choice: time for the LORD to act
alternatives: time to act for the LORD
decisions.reason: The words can mean that the time has come for the LORD himself to act, or that the time has come for people to act on his behalf. The first fits the plea of the stanza and the turn to "your" in the next line.
The verb has no named subject; it means people have broken God's instruction (compare verse 136).
Balanced and Readable name who has broken the instruction (m2).

records.gloss: Therefore I love your commands more than gold, and more than fine gold.
pieces: So I love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands above gold, above the finest gold.

L.127: Therefore I love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands more than gold, and more than fine gold.

R.127: So I love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands. I love them more than gold, even the very best gold.

decisions.choice: therefore: because God's instruction is broken
decisions.reason: "Therefore" links this line to verse 126: because others break God's instruction, the psalmist holds it dearer. Some take the word as simply emphatic.
The word (paz) is gold of the highest quality; Psalm 19:11 makes the same comparison.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֤ן׀כָּל־פִּקּ֣וּדֵי כֹ֣ל יִשָּׁ֑רְתִּי כָּל־אֹ֖רַח שֶׁ֣קֶר שָׂנֵֽאתִי׃
records.gloss: Therefore all precepts of everything I count right; every path of falsehood I hate.
pieces: So I hold all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts to be right in everything; I hate every road built on lies.

L.128: Therefore all the precepts of everything I count right; every path of falsehood I hate.

R.128: So I know that all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions are right in every way. I hate every way of life that is based on lies.

decisions.choice: all precepts of everything: all your precepts about everything
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "all precepts of all" is unusual. It most likely means God's precepts on every matter; the ancient Greek translation reads "all your precepts".

decisions.choice: count right: hold to be right, follow as straight
decisions.reason: The verb (yishsher) is to declare right or make straight.
Balanced and Readable say whose precepts they are, as the rest of the psalm does (m1).

decisions.choice: every road built on lies (B); every way of life that is based on lies (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as verse 104, which this line repeats.

records.gloss: Wonders [are] your testimonies; therefore my soul keeps them.
pieces: Your decrees are full of wonder; that is why I keep them with all my being.

L.129: Wonders [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies; therefore my soul keeps them.

R.129: What {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared is amazing. That is why I obey it with all my heart.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter pe, the seventeenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1).
The word (pela'ot) is used most often of God's mighty deeds (77:12, 15; verse 18). His testimonies are as wonderful as his works.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
with all my being (B); with all my heart (R)
decisions.reason: "My soul" (nefesh) is the psalmist himself, wholly committed.

records.gloss: [The] opening of your words gives light, giving understanding [to the] simple.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words are opened up, they shed light; they bring understanding to the naive.

L.130: The opening of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words gives light, giving understanding [to the] simple.

R.130: When {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words are explained, they are like a light. They help people who are easily fooled to understand.

decisions.reason: The word (petach) is an opening or doorway. It may mean the opening up of God's words to the mind, or the way in, as light comes through a door.

decisions.choice: the simple: the naive, those easily led
decisions.reason: The word (peta'im) is used in Proverbs for young, untaught people who believe anything (Proverbs 1:4; 14:15); see also 19:8.

records.gloss: My mouth I opened wide and panted, because for your commands I longed.
pieces: I gasp for breath with my mouth wide open, so deeply do I long for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

L.131: My mouth I opened wide, and I panted, for I longed for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

R.131: I want {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands so much that I am like someone gasping for air.

decisions.choice: opened my mouth and panted: eager longing
decisions.reason: The picture is of someone thirsty or out of breath, gasping for what he needs (compare 42:2).
The verb (ya'av) occurs only here; it is related to the verb "long" in verses 40 and 174.

records.gloss: Turn to me and be gracious to me, according to [the] custom toward those who love your name.
pieces: Turn toward me and be gracious, as is {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way with those who love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

L.132: Turn to me and be gracious to me, according to the custom toward those who love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

R.132: Look at me and be kind to me. That is what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do for people who love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: custom: what is right and usual
decisions.reason: Here mishpat means the rightful, customary way, not one of the words for God's law: God always treats those who love him with grace.
To love God's name is to love God as he has made himself known (5:12).
Balanced and Readable say whose custom it is.
Readable says "you" for "your name" (m2).

records.gloss: My steps make firm by your saying, and let not any iniquity rule over me.
pieces: Keep my steps steady by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word, and let no evil be master over me.

L.133: My steps make firm by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying, and let not any iniquity rule over me.

R.133: Guide each step I take by what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said. Do not let any kind of sin control me.

decisions.reason: The verb (hekhin) is to make firm or set in order.

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often a promise
decisions.reason: As in 119:103. Here it is God's word in general.
The word ('aven) is evil that does harm and brings trouble (5:6).

records.gloss: Redeem me from [the] oppression of humankind, so that I may keep your precepts.
pieces: Set me free when people oppress me, and I will keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

L.134: Redeem me from the oppression of {{gender:humankind|man}}, so that I may keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts.

R.134: Save me from people who treat me cruelly, so that I can obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions.

decisions.reason: The verb (padah) is to buy back or set free from slavery or danger.
The word ('adam) means people in general, set against God, whose help the psalmist seeks.
The word means human beings in general, so the default is inclusive, with the traditional "man" as the alternative.

records.gloss: Your face make shine on your servant, and teach me your statutes.
pieces: Turn the light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face toward {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, and train me in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

L.135: Your face make shine on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, and teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

R.135: Smile on me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, and teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.choice: make your face shine: the priests' blessing
decisions.reason: The words echo the blessing in Numbers 6:25 (also 4:7; 31:17; 80:4).

decisions.choice: face shine: look on with favor
decisions.reason: A shining face is a kind and favorable look.
Readable gives the sense of the picture (m2).

decisions.choice: statutes: what God has laid down

records.source: פַּלְגֵי־מַ֭יִם יָרְד֣וּ עֵינָ֑י עַ֝֗ל לֹא־שָׁמְר֥וּ תוֹרָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Streams of water my eyes have run down, because they have not kept your instruction.
pieces: My eyes pour out streams of water, because people do not keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

L.136: Streams of water my eyes have run down, because they have not kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction.

R.136: I cry and cry because people do not obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.choice: streams of water: floods of tears
decisions.reason: The psalmist weeps so much that his eyes run like streams (Lamentations 3:48).
As in verse 126, the verb has no named subject.
Balanced and Readable name who does not keep the instruction (m2).

records.gloss: Righteous [are] you, YHWH, and upright [are] your judgments.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are just in all {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings are straight and true.

R.137: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} always do what is right, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions are fair.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter tsade, the eighteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1).

decisions.choice: righteous and upright: just and straight
decisions.reason: Righteous (tsaddiq) is doing what is right; upright (yashar) is straight, without twist. The adjective "upright" is singular: each judgment is upright.
Balanced says how God is righteous: in what he does.

records.gloss: You have commanded righteousness [as] your testimonies, and faithfulness exceedingly.

records.gloss: I have kept your precepts and your testimonies, for all my ways [are] before you.
pieces: I keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decrees, for everything I do lies open before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.168: I have kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} testimonies, for all my ways [are] before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.168: I obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions and what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have declared, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see everything I do.

decisions.choice: testimonies: what God has solemnly declared
all my ways before you: God sees all I do
decisions.reason: The psalmist lives openly before God, who sees all his conduct (139:3).

records.source: תִּקְרַ֤ב רִנָּתִ֣י לְפָנֶ֣יךָ יְהוָ֑ה כִּדְבָרְךָ֥ הֲבִינֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: May my cry come near before you, YHWH; according to your word give me understanding.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, let my cry come close to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; give me understanding as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word has said.

L.169: Let my cry come near before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word give me understanding.

R.169: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please hear me when I cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Help me understand, as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word says.

decisions.reason: Each of the eight verses of this stanza begins with the letter taw, the twenty-second and last letter of the Hebrew alphabet (see 119:1). With this stanza the alphabet, and the psalm, is complete.
The word (rinnah) is a loud cry, of joy or, as here, of prayer (17:1).

records.gloss: May my plea come before you; according to your saying deliver me.
pieces: Let my prayer for mercy reach {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; rescue me as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have promised.

L.170: Let my plea come before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying deliver me.

R.170: Please listen when I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for mercy. Rescue me, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} promised.

decisions.reason: The word (techinnah) is a request for favor, from the verb "be gracious".

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often a promise
decisions.reason: As in 119:103. Here it is a promise.

records.source: תַּבַּ֣עְנָה שְׂפָתַ֣י תְּהִלָּ֑ה כִּ֖י תְלַמְּדֵ֣נִי חֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: May my lips pour forth praise, for you teach me your statutes.
pieces: Let praise bubble up from my lips, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

L.171: Let my lips pour forth praise, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} statutes.

R.171: I will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with words that pour out of me, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} laws.

decisions.choice: pour forth: bubble up like a spring
decisions.reason: The verb (hibbia') is used of a spring pouring out water, and of words pouring out (19:3; Proverbs 18:4).
The verbs in verses 169-175 can be wishes or statements; the wish fits the prayer of the stanza.

decisions.choice: statutes: what God has laid down

alternatives: let my lips pour forth praise
decisions.reason: Readable says it as the psalmist's own promise, which keeps the sense of the wish.

records.source: תַּ֣עַן לְ֭שׁוֹנִי אִמְרָתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֖י כָל־מִצְוֺתֶ֣יךָ צֶּֽדֶק׃
records.gloss: May my tongue sing [of] your saying, for all your commands [are] righteousness.
pieces: Let my tongue answer with songs about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word, since every command {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give is right.

L.172: Let my tongue sing [of] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saying, for all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands [are] righteousness.

R.172: I will sing about what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said, because all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands are right.

decisions.reason: The verb ('anah) can mean to answer or to sing (as one voice answers another).

decisions.choice: saying: what God has said, often a promise
decisions.reason: As in 119:103. Here it is God's word in general.
As in verse 171.

records.gloss: May your hand be to help me, for your precepts I have chosen.
pieces: Reach out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand to help me, since {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts are what I have chosen.

L.173: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand be [ready] to help me, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} precepts I have chosen.

R.173: Be ready to help me with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power, because I have chosen to follow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instructions.

decisions.reason: God's hand is his power to act.
Readable gives the sense of "hand" (m1).

records.gloss: I long for your salvation, YHWH, and your instruction [is] my delight.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I yearn for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to save me, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction is my joy.

L.174: I long for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction [is] my delight.

R.174: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I want so much for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to save me. Your teaching makes me glad.

decisions.reason: The verb (ta'av) is to long for (verse 40); verse 131 uses a related word.
As in verse 92 (sha'ashu'im): the deepest pleasure.

records.gloss: May my soul live, and it will praise you, and may your judgments help me.
pieces: Keep me alive to praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rulings come to my aid.

L.175: Let my soul live, and it will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments help me.

R.175: Keep me alive, and I will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} decisions help me.

decisions.reason: "My soul" (nefesh) is the psalmist himself.
The psalmist asks for life so that he may praise God; the living praise him (compare 6:6; 115:17-18).

records.source: תָּעִ֗יתִי כְּשֶׂ֣ה אֹ֭בֵד בַּקֵּ֣שׁ עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י מִ֝צְוֺתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א שָׁכָֽחְתִּי׃
records.gloss: I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek your servant, for your commands I have not forgotten.
pieces: Like a lost sheep I have wandered off; search for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, since {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands have not slipped from my mind.

L.176: I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands I have not forgotten.

R.176: I have wandered away like a sheep that is lost. Come and find me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, because I still remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} commands.

decisions.reason: The picture of God's people as straying sheep comes again in Isaiah 53:6 and Jeremiah 50:6, and Jesus tells of the shepherd who goes to look for the lost sheep (Luke 15:4-6).

decisions.choice: the psalm ends with a plea
decisions.reason: After 176 lines in praise of God's word, the psalm does not end in triumph but in a plea: the one who loves God's commands still needs God to come and find him.
The psalmist speaks of himself as God's servant ('eved), one who belongs to God and serves him.
